items.title: In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran unleashes a plot against the West years in the making
items.description: By moving so much of the war into the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf, Tehran has hit its adversaries where it hurts the most. Analysts warn that while the United States military is mighty, history shows in asymmetrical warfare, the lesser power can win the day.

items.title: Live: Thousands more US Marines to be deployed to Middle East, officials say
items.description: The White House claims it could "take out" Iran's strategically important Kharg Island "any time" that Donald Trump gives the order.

items.title: What experts say is likely to happen to Australia's fuel supply from mid-April
items.description: The government is responding to fuel shortages due to the war in the Middle East and says Australia has enough supply until mid-April. Here's what experts say could happen after that.

items.title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
items.description: Norris' epic fight with kung-fu superstar Bruce Lee in The Way of The Dragon helped him Norris into an icon, and he went on to star in more than 20 movies.

items.title: Federal politics is about to become all about the gas industry
items.description: Scott Morrison's assertion that the chase to secure vaccines in early 2021 was "not a race" cost him dearly. A similar global contest is already underway, only this time it involves securing energy supplies.

items.title: Live: Rivers rise in Queensland as cyclone to pick up steam ahead severe NT impact
items.description: The category two system is expected to strengthen today as it heads towards the Northern Territory. Follow live.

items.title: Polls open in South Australian election, after record number of early votes
items.description: South Australians head to the polls today for the 2026 state election, where One Nation could threaten the Liberal Party's status as the official opposition and Labor is expected to have a landslide victory.

items.title: Polls predict easy Labor win in SA, but One Nation will be closely watched
items.description: Both polls and pundits are expecting Labor to comfortably win today's election, but exactly who Labor will be beating — and who it will face in the next parliament — is the key question.

items.title: It's not as exciting as a royal visit, but something else happened in Tassie this week
items.description: It was a glamorous royal visit which dominated headlines in Tasmania this week, but some other — less glitzy — developments have the potential to rebuild the public's trust in the government.

items.title: Why I watch MAFS with my teenage son
items.description: Watching the largely fake, but also completely true, juggernaut reality TV series Married at First Sight with our 14-year-old was never a deliberate choice but it is potentially very powerful.

items.title: Matildas defender Kaitlyn Torpey is a goldfish, and it's taking her to new heights
items.description: A Ted Lasso lesson, and an Australian indie rock classic, are inspiring Kaitlyn Torpey to take her career to new heights, as she prepares for tonight's Women's Asian Cup final.

items.title: Earth's low orbit is becoming cluttered with high-velocity space junk
items.description: Thousands of satellites are being launched into space at low Earth orbit, joining hundreds of thousands of pieces of space junk, and it's becoming a real problem.

items.title: Iran war 'worst' time for tax, say gas companies
items.description: The Greens and One Nation are among those that want gas profits levied, with pressure mounting on Labor to respond to growing calls for reform.

items.title: Australian Olympic champ McEvoy breaks 17yo world record
items.description: Australia's Cameron McEvoy sets a world record in the men's 50 metres freestyle, dipping under the previous mark that had stood since 2009.

items.title: Norway's Crown Princess says she was 'deceived' by Epstein
items.description: Norway's Crown Princess has told national TV that she had been "manipulated and deceived" by Jeffrey Epstein and wished she had never met him.

items.title: Pair arrested after trying to enter naval base hosting UK's nuclear submarines
items.description: The man and woman were arrested after trying to enter HM Naval Base Clyde on Thursday, Scottish Police say.

items.title: Greig Fraser filmed the unfilmable for Dune. Now he's back for Project Hail Mary
items.description: With most of Project Hail Mary's action taking place in far off corners of space it was up to Australian cinematographer Greig Fraser to create what we've never seen.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of 2000s hip-hop, Mercury in retrograde and disturbing TV puppets
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Finding an escape from modern life in the booming world of arts and crafts
items.description: Craft trends come and go, but a resurgence in social arts and crafts is proving that creativity and human connection are still very much in vogue.

items.title: Bellamy pinpoints Storm's downfall as Broncos achieve 10-year first
items.description: Storm coach Craig Bellamy identifies the area in which he believes his side let themselves down, as the Broncos celebrate a rare win in Melbourne.

items.title: Bulldogs 'tick off' another item on 2026 AFL season bucket list
items.description: A brilliant Oskar Baker goal clinches a thrilling win for the Bulldogs over the Crows, leaving Luke Beveridge's side unbeaten after three matches.

items.title: Why our first major aviation disaster remained a mystery for 27 years
items.description: When eight people vanished without a trace in 1931, Australia's first major airline disaster became a 27-year mystery that gripped the nation, until a hiker's chance discovery changed everything.

items.title: Donor devastated as charity plans to sell land despite agreement not to
items.description: A charity known for the landmark separation of conjoined twins Krishna and Trishna lists a regional Victorian property for sale against the wishes of its donor.

items.title: Running out of fuel creates 'triple whammy' for farmer
items.description: Scott Worthington has run out of fuel, after first running out of water on his drought-stricken farm, and watching his pastures turn to dirt.

items.title: One Nation volunteers accused of illegally filling out how-to-vote cards
items.description: Candidates in two separate seats in the South Australia state election complain that One Nation volunteers are writing in preferences on how-to-vote cards, despite the party's approved cards not including any preferences beyond 1 for One Nation.
